core.title: Keep each feature at 8 components or fewer; split it otherwise
core.given: A planner is defining or extending a feature and its list of components in the plan artifacts.
core.when: The feature's component count would reach more than 8.
core.then: Keep the feature at ≤ 8 components; if more components are needed, split the feature into smaller features instead of exceeding 8.
prefer: Use the typical 8-component budget as a guide: about 2 frontend-side components, 3 backend-side components and 3 shared cross-cutting components; the layer roles each side's components live in come from the profile's side-to-layer mapping.
When a 9th component is needed, split the feature along a cohesive boundary into separate features, each within the limit.
avoid: Planning a feature with more than 8 components (e.g. 12) and letting it sprawl instead of splitting.
Gaming the count by merging unrelated responsibilities into one component or hiding components outside the feature just to stay at 8.
core.why: A hard ceiling of 8 components keeps features cohesive and bounded, mirroring the acceptance limits of the plan artifacts; more than 8 signals the feature is too large and should be split.
evidence: Count the components declared for each feature in the plan artifacts; every feature has ≤ 8.
The stack's component-count check passes for the planned features.
Any feature that needed more than 8 components appears as multiple split features.
verification: A count check scans the plan artifacts and counts the components declared per feature; every feature must declare at most 8. The threshold is inclusive: 8 passes, 9 or more is reported as a finding.
The typical distribution (about 2 frontend-side, 3 backend-side, 3 shared components) is guidance only; the check does not enforce any particular distribution.

Layers per side: frontend-side components live in the layer roles the profile assigns to the frontend side, backend-side components in the layer roles the profile assigns to the backend side, and shared components are cross-cutting concerns.

The check only counts declared components; it cannot detect count-gaming (unrelated responsibilities merged into one component, or components hidden outside the feature), which stays planner judgment, nor does it judge whether a split boundary is cohesive.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: the check reports findings, it does not hard-fail.

fires: Planner writes a feature plan that lists 9 or more components
Planner adds a component to a feature that already has 8 components
doesNotFire: Feature with exactly 8 components (e.g. 2 frontend + 3 backend + 3 shared)
Editing component internals without changing the number of components in a feature

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's local name for the plan artifacts in which features and their components are declared and whose acceptance limits the rule's rationale mirrors; the count check scans these artifacts.

The layer roles in which each side's components live: the layers occupied by frontend-side and backend-side components, and what shared components count as; instantiates the typical-budget guidance and the layers-per-side description.
profileRequirements.bunValue: frontend -> presentation, application; backend -> application, domain, integration; shared -> cross-cutting concerns

proposedKeys.meaning: The layer roles in which each side's components live: which layers frontend-side and backend-side components occupy, and what shared components count as.
proposedKeys.bunValue: frontend -> presentation, application; backend -> application, domain, integration; shared -> cross-cutting concerns
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.layers lists the stack's layer roles in dependency order with their local names; it does not map product sides (frontend, backend, shared) to groups of layer roles, and no other vocabulary key covers side-to-layer grouping.

bunOnly.reason: WMBT is the Bun stack's local name for its plan artifact; the core refers to plan artifacts generically and the local name is supplied by the profile (roles.plan_artifact.name).

bunOnly.text: Threshold max_per_feature = 8 (inclusive: 8 passes, 9+ is a finding).
bunOnly.reason: 'max_per_feature' is this rule's source term id, a realization identifier; the core states the threshold itself (8, inclusive) in core:verification without the id.

bunOnly.text: Validator test_component_count_limit::test_component_count_limit passes for the planned features.
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun validator id of this rule; per the derivation rules the validator id is a realization detail and the core names the check generically.

bunOnly.text: note: "Needs an observer that counts components declared per feature in the plan artifacts (the validator test_component_count_limit already does this count)."
bunOnly.reason: The observability note references the Bun validator id; the core keeps the fact and its observability without the realization-specific note.

classification.note: Planner, feature and components are plan-level concepts with no stack machinery; only 'the plan' was generalized to 'the plan artifacts' role.
The single obligation: ≤ 8 components, split instead of exceeding; already neutral.
Rationale is neutral except 'WMBT', the Bun local name of the plan artifact, which is concretized by the profile and kept as a bunOnly fragment.

The 8-component budget and the typical 2/3/3 split are rule data and stay in the core; the concrete side-to-layer assignment (which layer roles each side's components live in) is stack architecture supplied by the profile key, no longer hardcoded in the core.
Sprawl counter-example with a neutral count example (12).
Count-gaming guidance stays agent-facing advice; its non-detectability by the count check is recorded as a verification non-coverage note.
Counting components per feature in the plan artifacts; neutral, no path or artifact kind named.
Neutralized to 'the stack's component-count check passes'; the validator id test_component_count_limit::test_component_count_limit is a realization detail.
Split features appear as multiple features within the limit; already neutral.
Threshold semantics (8 inclusive, 9+ is a finding) go to verification; the source term id 'max_per_feature' is a realization identifier kept in bunOnly.

Only the numeric typical distribution (frontend 2, backend 3, shared 3) is explicitly non-enforced guidance, exactly as the Bun text says; the side-to-layer definitions inside this detail (frontend = presentation + application, backend = application + domain + integration, shared = cross-cutting) are stack architecture carried by the profile key, not by the core.

The layers-per-side description is restated in core:verification parameterized by the profile's side-to-layer mapping, as a plain statement of where components live with no added enforcement or non-enforcement qualifier (the previous 'guidance, not a separate finding' exemption was removed as an addition the Bun text does not make). The concrete assignment (frontend -> presentation/application, backend -> application/domain/integration) is the profile value. roles.layers is deliberately not used: its documented meaning is the ordered layer-role list with local names, which this rule does not consume.
Per-rule severity and disposition stay with the rule: advisory, severity 2, report findings without hard-failing.
Task terms are per-rule activation data; 'wagon' (a bounded slice of the product) and 'plan' belong to the shared planning vocabulary, not to a runtime or framework.
Fact (change: component added / component list edited, needs_new_observer) is neutral; the note's validator id is a realization detail kept in bunOnly.
Finding fact 'component_count > 8' with needs_new_observer; already neutral (each stack must surface its count-limit validator result to the planner).

neutralityNotes: The obligation is a planning-level quantity rule; no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path appears in the core. The ceiling (8) and the typical 2/3/3 distribution are rule data, not stack facts, so they stay in the core. 'Frontend/backend/shared' are product-architecture sides; which layer roles each side's components live in is stack architecture and is now supplied by the profile through the proposed key roles.layers_per_side (revision 2: the concrete mapping was removed from core.prefer[0] and core.verification). roles.layers is not referenced at all: its documented meaning is the ordered layer-role list with local names, which this rule does not consume. Also in revision 2, the added 'guidance, not a separate finding' exemption on the layers-per-side description was dropped; the core now states where components live plainly, as bun.json does, and only the typical numeric distribution remains explicitly non-enforced, matching the Bun text. The activation facts for change and finding are marked needs_new_observer: every realization must provide its own observer that counts components per feature in its plan artifacts and surfaces the count-limit finding to the planner. The remaining Bun-specific content is identificational: the plan-artifact local name 'WMBT' (profile roles.plan_artifact.name) and this rule's validator and source-term ids (bunOnly).
